panels.description:
What it shows: Number of connections sitting free in the pool

Simple meaning: Ready-to-use connections waiting for next request

Good sign: Having idle connections means you have capacity for more requests
panels.title: Idle Connections

panels.description:
What it shows: How much of the connection pool is being used

Simple meaning: If you have 60,000 connections available and 2 are active, this shows 0.003%

When to worry: Above 80% means pool is almost full, requests will start waiting
panels.title: Pool Utilization %

panels.description:
What it shows: Number of connections currently making API calls





Simple meaning: Right now, how many connections are busy talking to OAuth/Wallet/PostPaid


Example: oauth-pool: 2 means 2 connections are calling OAuth API right now
panels.title: Active Connections

panels.description:
What it shows: Connections created so far by Reactor Netty

Simple meaning: Pool creates connections on-demand, not all at once

Example: Shows 2 means only 2 connections have been created (out of 60,000 possible)
panels.title: Total Allocated

panels.description:
What it shows: Requests waiting because no connection is available

Simple meaning: Traffic jam! Requests are stuck in queue

Action needed: If > 0, increase pool size immediately!
panels.title: Pending Requests 🚨

panels.description:
What it shows: Maximum connections allowed (from your config)

Simple meaning: The limit you set in application.properties

Example: oauth: 60,000 means you can have up to 60,000 connections
panels.title: Max Capacity

panels.description:
What it shows: Connections currently running SQL queries

Simple meaning: How many database queries are happening right now

Example: config_database: 6 means 6 queries running
panels.title: DB Active Connections

panels.description:
What it shows: What % of max capacity has been allocated

Simple meaning: (Allocated ÷ Max Capacity) × 100

Example: 0.003% means very efficient - only creating what's needed
panels.title: Allocation Efficiency %

panels.description:
What it shows: How much of DB connection pool is being used

Simple meaning: If you have 30 DB connections and 6 are active, this shows 20%

When to worry: Above 85% means DB pool is almost full
panels.title: DB Pool Utilization %

panels.description:
What it shows: Queries waiting because no DB connection available

Simple meaning: Database queries stuck in queue

Action needed: If > 5, increase DB pool size!
panels.title: DB Pending Requests 🚨

panels.description:
What it shows: Free database connections in pool

Simple meaning: Ready connections waiting for next query

Good sign: Having idle DB connections means you have capacity
panels.title: DB Idle Connections

panels.description:
What it shows: Total DB pool size (from your config)

Simple meaning: config_database: 30 means you have 30 DB connections

Note: R2DBC creates all connections at startup (unlike WebClient)
panels.title: DB Total Connections

panels.description:
What it shows: How often Minor GC happens (events per second)

Simple meaning: If 0.5/sec, GC runs every 2 seconds

When to worry: Above 1/sec means too frequent, wasting CPU
panels.title: Young GC Frequency

panels.description:
What it shows: How long Minor GC (young generation) pauses your app

Simple meaning: Time your app freezes to clean up short-lived objects

Impact: During this time, no requests are processed

When to worry: Above 100ms means noticeable delay
panels.title: Young GC Pause Time

panels.description:
What it shows: How long Full GC (old generation) pauses your app

Simple meaning: Time your app completely stops (Stop-The-World event!)

Impact: ALL requests are blocked during this time

When to worry: Above 500ms is critical! Users will notice!
panels.title: Old GC Pause Time 🚨

panels.description:
What it shows: Total Full GC events since JVM started

Simple meaning: Should be low! Ideally 0 or very few

When to worry: If increasing rapidly, you have memory issues
panels.title: Old GC Total Count

panels.description:
What it shows: How often Full GC happens (events per second)

Simple meaning: Should be very rare! If > 0.1/sec, possible memory leak

When to worry: Any frequent Full GC is bad - investigate immediately!
panels.title: Old GC Frequency

panels.description:
What it shows: Total Minor GC events since JVM started

Simple meaning: Counter that keeps increasing

Use: Track GC frequency trends over time
panels.title: Young GC Total Count

panels.description:
What it shows: How much heap memory is currently in use

Simple meaning: Memory holding your application objects right now

Example: 512 MB means 512 MB of objects in memory
panels.title: Heap Memory Used

panels.description:
What it shows: Total milliseconds spent in GC since JVM started

Simple meaning: Cumulative time your app was paused for garbage collection

Example: 5000ms means app was paused for 5 seconds total since startup
panels.title: Total GC Time

panels.description:
What it shows: What % of time is spent doing garbage collection

Simple meaning: If 5%, then out of every 100ms, 5ms is GC

When to worry: Above 10% means GC is eating too much time
panels.title: GC Overhead %

panels.description:
Simple Description:
How many client connections are currently active and processing requests

What It Means:
- Normal: Varies with load (0-100s under normal traffic)
- High: > 1000 (heavy traffic or slow responses causing connection buildup)

Why It Matters:
Shows real-time load on your server
panels.title: HTTP Server Active Connections

panels.description:
Simple Description:
How many reactor-http-nio threads are running to handle incoming API requests

What It Means:
- Normal: 8-16 threads (depends on CPU cores)
- High: > 32 threads (unusual, check configuration)

Why It Matters:
These threads handle ALL incoming HTTP requests in your WebFlux app
panels.title: NIO Thread Count

panels.description:
What it shows: How many CPU cores each container is actively using
Result format: 1.19 cores (absolute number)
Use case: Primary metric for capacity planning
Best for: Understanding actual CPU consumption
Alert threshold: > 3.5 cores (70% of 5 allocated cores)
panels.title: CPU Cores Used - Per Container

panels.description:
What it shows: How many CPU cores each container is actively using
Result format: 1.19 cores (absolute number)
Use case: Primary metric for capacity planning
Best for: Understanding actual CPU consumption
Alert threshold: > 3.5 cores (70% of 5 allocated cores)
panels.title: CPU Cores Used - Per Container

panels.description:
<0 = Under limit ✅
0 = At limit exactly 🟡
>0 = Over limit = Throttling! 🔴
panels.title: CPU Usage Exceeding Limit

panels.description:
<0 = Under limit ✅
0 = At limit exactly 🟡
>0 = Over limit = Throttling! 🔴
panels.title: If result > 100% → Throttling confirmed! CPU

panels.description:
Simple Description:
How long (in nanoseconds) the event loop is busy processing

What It Means:
- Measures CPU time spent by NIO threads
- Higher value = threads are working more

Why It Matters:
If this is constantly high with high pending tasks, you have a problem
panels.title: Event Loop Busy Time

panels.description:
Simple Description:
Total number of connections created since server started

What It Means:
- Always increasing (counter metric)
- Use rate() to see connections per second

Why It Matters:
Track connection rate over time to understand traffic patterns
panels.title: HTTP Server Total Connections

panels.description:
Simple Description:
How many tasks are waiting in the event loop queue

What It Means:
- Good: 0-5 tasks (event loop is keeping up)
- Warning: 10-50 tasks (event loop getting busy)
- Critical: > 50 tasks (blocking operations or CPU saturation)

Why It Matters:
⚠️ High pending tasks = Your NIO threads are blocked or overloaded
This directly increases latency!
panels.title: Event Loop Pending Tasks

panels.description:
Simple Description:
How many tasks are waiting because all boundedElastic threads are busy

What It Means:
- Good: 0 tasks (threads are available)
- Warning: 10-50 tasks (threads getting saturated)
- Critical: > 100 tasks (thread starvation, will increase latency)

Why It Matters:
⚠️ High queued tasks = Your app is doing too much blocking work
Need to optimize or increase thread pool size
panels.title: BoundedElastic Queued Tasks

panels.description:
Simple Description:
How many boundedElastic threads are currently working on blocking operations

What It Means:
- Normal: 0-20 threads (depends on cache updates, DB calls during startup)
- High: > 50 threads (too many blocking operations)

Why It Matters:
Shows if you're doing blocking work correctly on boundedElastic (not on NIO threads)
panels.title: BoundedElastic Active Threads

panels.description:
Simple Description:
Total number of threads available in the boundedElastic pool

What It Means:
- Configured in application.properties
- Default: 10 x CPU cores (e.g., 80 threads for 8 cores)

Why It Matters:
Compare with active threads to see if you're running out of capacity
panels.title: BoundedElastic Pool Size

panels.description:
Simple Description:
Percentage of boundedElastic threads currently in use (0-100%)

What It Means:
- Good: 0-50% (plenty of capacity)
- Warning: 50-80% (getting busy)
- Critical: > 80% (near capacity, risk of queuing)

Why It Matters:
Easy way to see if you need more boundedElastic threads
panels.title: BoundedElastic Utilization
